fieldValues.title: A remedy names who it serves
fieldValues.decision_question: Does a remedy say who it is a remedy for, or only which problem it answers?
fieldValues.context: In the method package a remedy answers a problem (com.semanticops.method/answers), and the remedy type's fields (move, does not fix, falsifier, source, look again when) name no one. Ratified decision 708c9373 models a problem that occurs in several domains as one problem held by one persona-in-domain in each, with the problem's domains derived from its holders and never stored. The exercise 'How a remedy differs by domain and persona' (2026-10-16) asked what follows for remedies. The owner answered the same day: "A remedy does need to point to who it is a remedy for. (One man's poison...)". On 2026-11-09 the owner found remedies eeefe987 and 6a45944b sitting 'In no domain' because no persona-in-domain holds the problems they answer: "Found them. They are not on firm ground." (vignette 19dec106).
fieldValues.friction: A remedy for a problem held in two domains reads as fitting both, though what helps one persona may harm another. A remedy whose problem has no holder floats with no domain and nothing shows it. An affirmed remedy already tends to read as the right one for everyone (SP-128).
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: 1. A remedy names the persona-in-domain it serves, taken from the holders of the problem it answers (chosen; the mechanism, a relation or arrangement in a domain container, is still to be compared). 2. Derive who a remedy serves from its problem's holders only, as today: needs nothing new, but cannot say a remedy suits one holder and not another, and a holder-less problem leaves the remedy unanchored. 3. Clone the problem per domain when remedies diverge: keeps remedies simple, but splits one claim into copies, against 708c9373. 4. Place remedies under their problems in each domain container's outline: shows grouping, but arrangement is layout, not a semantic claim. 5. Do nothing: remedies stay scoped by implication and the 'in no domain' cases keep appearing.
fieldValues.key_requirements: Meaning that must stay stable is stated as a relation or field, not as container membership. It must stay consistent with 708c9373: a remedy names a persona-in-domain, never a bare domain, and that persona-in-domain holds the problem the remedy answers, so there is no second path to a domain that could disagree with the first. The practice is still being learnt (vignette 76f63499): the owner asked to weigh containers against relations before picking a mechanism ("We should investigate the pros and cons. We can do both."), and draft 4a67caf5 may change what a domain is. The owner's separate remark on cloning problems ("We can clone problems, as long as we keep a link between them") is not decided here, because it sits against 708c9373.
fieldValues.decision_statement: A remedy names the persona-in-domain it serves, chosen from the holders of the problem it answers.
fieldValues.rationale: What helps depends on who is helped, so a remedy without a named recipient overclaims. Choosing the recipient from the problem's holders keeps 708c9373's derivation intact, and makes a remedy whose problem has no holder visibly unanchored instead of silently domain-less. It also gives SP-128 a check: an affirmed remedy is affirmed for someone, not for everyone.
fieldValues.revisit_when: Remedies routinely serve every holder of their problem alike, so that naming one becomes noise; or the chosen mechanism lets a remedy name someone who does not hold its problem; or draft 4a67caf5 changes what a persona-in-domain is.
fieldValues.next_steps: The mechanism comparison (relation against container outline) stays open on the exercise; the method-package change follows as a linked issue once it is chosen.
